name: RoleAgent
abstract: RoleAgent benchmarks the building and interaction quality of role-playing agents. This page uses General Response WR-H on the English setting as the primary leaderboard.
contributions: The paper does not report one unified overall score, so the page uses the most user-facing human win rate as the primary leaderboard.
Self-knowledge and reaction are also preserved to reflect the structure of role-agent ability.
method: RoleAgent aims to automatically build high-quality role-playing agents from raw scripts without manual profile creation.
In the building stage, it parses scripts and constructs a hierarchical memory system for each role.
In the interaction stage, it improves conversations through query decomposition, memory retrieval, summarization, and response generation.
The paper also introduces RoleAgentBench to evaluate self-knowledge, reaction, general response, and summarization ability.
Its core contribution is combining scalable script-based role construction with a systematic evaluation benchmark.

metrics.name: General Response WR-H
metrics.note: Human win rate on general response quality.

leaderboard_note: The primary leaderboard uses General Response WR-H from the English evaluation subset. Since the paper emphasizes multi-dimensional role-agent ability, a few auxiliary metrics are kept as well.
